verdict_reason: 4 reproducible mandatory counterexamples (F1-F4); the r7 frozen parameters themselves are inside the allow list and the scientific values did not move, the defects are in the code control flow

frozen_identity.shm_note: the -shm index file mtime advanced (a read-only attachment to a WAL database does that, demonstrated); its sha256 did not change, no zero-write claim is made

mandatory_findings.title: the final 'completed' commit is not covered by the 450 s per-run deadline
mandatory_findings.counterexample: real wall clock: deadline 20 s, the final commit took 21 s more -> run recorded 'completed', wall_seconds 24.81 > 20; the same overrun inside the last gradient aborts (control)
mandatory_findings.decision_requirement: S1-R7-DECISION item 5: the last-step IO / ledger.finish commit taking more than 450 s must also not be completed
mandatory_findings.author_gap: the r7 deadline controls cover last-gradient / duty-sleep / checkpoint-io / metadata-io / exact-boundary but not ledger.finish

mandatory_findings.title: the r7 phase accounting refuses three states the S1 product itself writes
mandatory_findings.counterexample: a legitimate 'collecting' / 'validating' / 'stopping' row is refused as an unknown state -> phase_total_wall_seconds raises -> the train/eval entry refuses with the misleading stage 'ledger_timestamp_invalid' instead of counting the row
mandatory_findings.decision_requirement: every phase-related prep/train/eval/verify row must be counted
mandatory_findings.author_gap: the r7 phase-accounting test only uses 'completed' and a made-up 'quarantined' state

mandatory_findings.title: the arm1 (D candidate) evaluation entry cannot complete with the real frozen r7 document
mandatory_findings.counterexample: the arm1 experiment is registered with arm1_deadline_seconds=2 while the run is registered with the entry's 300 s eval budget -> 'run budget exceeds experiment run limits' (status failed, no run, no forward); with a budget <= 2 s the pre-reservation (>= 5 s) exceeds the run wall -> 'BudgetExceeded: wall_time_budget' (status stopped, an arm1 ledger row is burned without any evaluation)
mandatory_findings.decision_requirement: the registered single C0 re-verification path must work for the frozen D candidate
mandatory_findings.author_gap: the r7 D test never runs run_worker(eval, arm1) to completion with the real document; its fixture document has arm1_deadline_seconds=15

mandatory_findings.title: the 'one D evaluation run' limit is not enforced
mandatory_findings.counterexample: the arm1 evaluation run is opened without arm_id in its config snapshot while the guard filters on config_snapshot['arm_id']=='arm1' -> the second arm1 evaluation was not refused and the central ledger holds two completed arm1 evaluation rows
mandatory_findings.decision_requirement: the D candidate may be re-verified exactly once (d_candidate_eval_runs=1)
mandatory_findings.author_gap: the r7 test fabricates an arm_id='arm1' row that the product never creates

disclosed_findings.title: the report's refused_states list is wider than the implementation
disclosed_findings.detail: max(0.0, float(value)) normalises a NaN (or -inf) reservation to 0 (Python's max(0.0, nan) is 0.0) so the following isfinite guard can never fire; a finite far-future timestamp is accepted with the elapsed part charged as 0; not reachable from the real ledger (SQLite stores NaN as NULL, NOT NULL + CHECK reject it), but the card requires that unknown/non-compliant fields are never treated as 0

disclosed_findings.title: unfrozen identity of the trust root and of the ledger implementation
disclosed_findings.detail: the preregistration binds 14 source files; src/ainerzero/runtime/lifecycle.py (unchanged by the authors, sha 22ded55c...), the A2 baseline manifest (the D candidate trust root), src/ainerzero/learning/pilot_model.py and src/ainerzero/runtime/checkpoints.py are not bound; verify_d_candidate_identity computes a 'digest' that is never read (AST checked) and only reports the registered 3481b6ad... as a hint

disclosed_findings.title: the r7 D-candidate test states 'No MLX is imported here' but arms.py imports mlx.core at module level
disclosed_findings.detail: the review therefore injected a stub mlx package; the 7 failing tests are stub artefacts and were reported as unverified, not as failures

disclosed_findings.title: run_worker's train branch does not forward a CPU substitute to _train
disclosed_findings.detail: the production train path always uses runtime.MlxBackend, so the CPU evidence (the author's and the reviewer's) is at the _train level only; the real run_worker train path is not verifiable under the CPU-only constraint

tests/v9/experiments.note: the 7 failures are stub artefacts (no_update x2, pacer_duty x4, timing_sequence x1); they drive the real MLX runtime and were not re-run under the CPU-only constraint

tests/v9/geometry+contracts+teachers+tok.note: 2 of them assert that no mlx module is imported and were re-run without the stub
